fullName: SSC Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination (CHSL)
overview: SSC CHSL is the Staff Selection Commission's entry-level exam for **Group C posts** open to **12th-pass candidates** — Lower Divisional Clerk (LDC), Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA) and Data Entry Operator (DEO) across central ministries, departments and statutory bodies. There is no interview: selection runs through **two computer-based tiers**, a qualifying **typing or data-entry skill test**, and document verification. The exam rewards **speed and accuracy on a fixed syllabus** — basic arithmetic, reasoning, English and general awareness — which is why short formulas, topic drills and timed mocks beat open-ended reading. Note the design: **Tier 1 only shortlists you; the merit list is built from Tier 2 Sections I and II (360 marks)**, while the computer test and typing/skill test are qualifying hurdles you must clear.

stages.name: Tier 1 — Computer Based Exam
stages.notes: The notice sets a **sectional timer of 15 minutes for each subject** within the 60-minute paper, so you cannot carry unused time from one subject to another. Candidates eligible for a scribe get 80 minutes (20 per subject). Minimum qualifying marks in Tier 1 are **30% for UR, 25% for OBC/EWS and 20% for all other categories**. Scores are normalised when the exam runs in multiple shifts. Tier 1 only decides who is shortlisted for Tier 2.

stages.name: Tier 2 — Session I (objective) + Session II (skill/typing test)
stages.mode: Online CBT, two sessions on the same day

stages.notes: **Session I (2 h 15 min):** Section I is 1 hour (30 minutes sectional timer each for Maths and Reasoning), Section II is 1 hour (40 minutes for English, 20 minutes for GA), Section III is 15 minutes. **Session II — Section IV — is the Skill Test/Typing Test, qualifying only:** DEO posts take a 15-minute data-entry skill test (15,000 key depressions/hour for DEOs in the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, SSC and the Ministry of Culture; 8,000 key depressions/hour for other DEOs), and LDC/JSA candidates take a 10-minute typing test at **35 w.p.m. in English or 30 w.p.m. in Hindi** (Mangal font). Merit uses the **360 marks of Sections I and II only**; you must qualify in all sections. Minimum qualifying marks in Sections I, II and III are 30% UR, 25% OBC/EWS and 20% others. Negative marking of 1 applies in Sections I, II and III.

eligibility.nationality: Citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka or the listed East African countries and Vietnam with the intention of settling permanently in India. selectionProcess: **Tier 1 (shortlisting) → Tier 2 Sections I–III (objective) → Section IV skill/typing test → options and preferences → Document Verification by the user department.** Tier 1 decides who is called for Tier 2. The merit list is prepared on the **aggregate of Tier 2 Section I and Section II marks only**, provided you qualify Section III (Computer Knowledge Test) and Section IV (typing or skill test). Posts are then allotted on merit-cum-preference — the first available preference you filled is the one you get, and options are irreversible, so choose carefully. Ties are broken in this order: Tier 2 Section I marks, Tier 1 marks, then date of birth (older candidate ranks higher). **There is no interview.**
normalization: When an exam runs in many shifts with different question papers, SSC **normalises scores** using the procedure it published in its notice of 2 June 2025, and the normalised score is used for cut-offs and merit. Practical consequences: (1) never compare raw marks across shifts or years; (2) attempt according to the paper in front of you rather than chasing a number; (3) your normalised score — not the raw one — decides your result.

faqs.q: Do Tier 1 marks count towards final selection?
faqs.a: No. Tier 1 only shortlists candidates for Tier 2, although it is the third tie-break after Tier 2 Section I marks. The merit list is built from **Tier 2 Section I and Section II (360 marks)**.

faqs.q: What is the Tier 1 pattern and negative marking?
faqs.a: **100 questions, 200 marks, 60 minutes**, with 25 questions each in English, General Intelligence, Quantitative Aptitude and General Awareness. Each correct answer earns 2 marks and each wrong one costs **0.50**. Every subject has its own **15-minute sectional timer**.

Session I has **Section I** (Maths 30 Q + Reasoning 30 Q, 1 hour), **Section II** (English 40 Q + GA 20 Q, 1 hour) and **Section III** (Computer Knowledge, 15 Q, 15 minutes). Each question is 3 marks with −1 for a wrong answer. Session II is the skill or typing test. Merit marks come only from Sections I and II.

faqs.q: Is the computer test or typing test counted in merit?
faqs.a: No — both are **qualifying only**. The Computer Knowledge Test (Section III) and the Skill/Typing Test (Section IV) must be cleared, but their marks do not add to your merit score.

faqs.q: What typing speed is needed for LDC/JSA?
faqs.a: **35 words per minute in English** or **30 w.p.m. in Hindi**, tested over 10 minutes on a given passage. These correspond to roughly 10,500 and 9,000 key depressions per hour. You choose English or Hindi in the application form and cannot change it later; Hindi must be typed in Mangal font.

faqs.q: What does the DEO skill test require?
faqs.a: A 15-minute data-entry test. For DEOs in the Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, SSC and Culture ministries the required speed is **15,000 key depressions per hour**; for other DEOs it is **8,000 key depressions per hour**. The skill test is mandatory for every DEO candidate.

faqs.q: Who can apply for DEO posts requiring Science and Maths?
faqs.a: Only 12th-pass candidates with **Science stream and Mathematics as a subject** are eligible for DEO/DEO Grade 'A' posts in the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, Staff Selection Commission and Ministry of Culture. For all other CHSL posts, any stream is fine.

In Tier 1 and in Tier 2 Sections I, II and III, minimum qualifying marks are **30% for UR, 25% for OBC/EWS and 20% for all other categories**. These are only floors — actual cut-offs depend on vacancies and difficulty.

Yes, candidates who have appeared in 12th can apply, but they must hold the qualification on or before the cut-off date (**7 October 2026** this cycle), and the Board must have declared the result by then. Without a passing result by that date, the candidature is rejected.

faqs.q: What is the age limit and fee?
faqs.a: Age limit is **18–27 years as on 1 August 2026**, with category relaxations. The fee is **₹100**; women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen candidates pay nothing. If you object to an answer key, the notice sets a charge of ₹50 per question.

faqs.q: Is there a waiting list or any interview?
faqs.a: There is **no interview**. SSC does not keep a waiting list for multi-post exams, but it uses a **sliding mechanism** for allocation, so qualifying candidates can move to a lower preference if higher ones fill up.

documents: Document verification is done by the user ministry or department **after the final result**. Keep these ready in original plus photocopies: **matriculation/secondary certificate** (date-of-birth proof), **12th pass certificate or marksheet** (educational qualification), **category certificate** (SC/ST/OBC-non-creamy-layer/EWS in the prescribed format; EWS needs an income and asset certificate valid for FY 2026-27), **PwBD or ex-servicemen documents** where applicable, proof for any age relaxation claimed, a **No Objection Certificate** if you are already employed in government service, and documents for any name change after matriculation (marriage certificate, affidavit, gazette notification). If a claim in your application is not backed by the right certificate at verification, your candidature is cancelled.
